trend_qty_title: Premium accounts for 1,191 of the 2,371 units sold in January
structure_intro_title: Premium range at NZ$41,785.60, or 47.2% of store revenue
category_mix_title: Supplements lead on both revenue (30.1%) and units (32.6%)
premium_mix_title: Honey at 31.5% of premium revenue from 16.2% of premium units
top_products_title: Three premium lines in the top 10 SKUs by units
brand_title: Clearfield leads the store brand table at 8.7% of revenue
milk_brand_title: Clearfield holds 32.0% of milk powder against Ambervale at 20.9%
milk_brand_note: Clearfield at 32.0% and Ambervale at 20.9% together cover just over half the category, with Westbrook at 4.3% the smallest of the six listed. Facings for the two leaders should reflect that gap when the shelf is reset.
pickup_title: Pickup skews regular: NZ$9,737.10 against NZ$2,051.28 premium
pickup_comment: Pickup orders carried 161 regular units and 35 premium units in January. Placing a small premium display at the collection point would put that range in front of customers who are already in store.
functional_title: Fish oil tops functional lines at NZ$4,194.93 on 126 units
functional_note: Fish oil (126 units) and joint care (100 units) are the two largest functional lines, while eye care and magnesium sit at 38 units each. Shelf space at eye level could follow that order.
channel_title: Export 1,265 units to local 1,100 in January
channel_comment: Export took 53.5% of units and NZ$54,322.26 of revenue, against NZ$34,990.18 local. The New Year holidays at the start of the month typically leave walk-in trade quiet, which may sit behind the local figure.
concentration_title: Top three SKU deciles carry 62.8% of revenue
operations_title: 268 visits and 94 mini-programme leads at a 61.0% completion rate
campaign_title: Summer bundle running on premium supplements
